project_type: Python security assessment toolkit (Bug Bounty Arsenal)
test_framework: No formal test framework - verification via python -m module execution
verification_instructions: 1. Run 'python -m super_monster --help' to verify CLI works. 2. Run 'python -m super_monster full --input ./monster_output/reports --output ./super_output' to verify pipeline. 3. Verify all imports work with 'python -c "from super_monster import correlator, retester, prioritizer, finding_db, attack_planner, diff_engine, notification, reporter"'
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET network mode. Python 3.11 available. No external APIs - all AI/scoring is rule-based. Pure Python standard library + colorama only.
contribution_requirements: Professional colored terminal output using colorama. All output must be actionable for bug bounty. Must work with python -m super_monster. Must integrate with Monster's JSON output format.
key_patterns: Monster uses dataclass Finding(finding_type, severity, title, description, url, evidence, remediation, cvss_score, cwe_id). Monster JSON output has report_metadata, executive_summary, findings[], recon_summary sections. Uses ColorOutput class from utils for colored terminal output. CLI uses argparse with subcommands. Modules are standalone .py files in package directory with __main__.py entry point.
directory_structure: Bug-Bounty/ contains: README.md (main), requirements.txt, monster/ (23k lines, web scanner), apk_analyzer/ (4.5k lines, mobile analysis), monster_output/reports/ (sample JSON/MD/HTML reports). New super_monster/ package to be created at same level as monster/.
